generation.input_rng: NumPy default_rng(281419); every actual input array is stored in the NPZ fixture.
procedure: Check out both exact commits and add reference root, reference utils and Manopt manopt subtree to the MATLAB/Octave path.

For each case read its *_initial and *_observations arrays from the NPZ fixture; observations are column-wise. Transfer these arrays to a MAT file using scipy.io.savemat without changing their values.
Construct great(n,k,window); use K=inner_steps and alpha=stepsize except when default_controls is true. JSON null stepsize maps to MATLAB []. Initialize with *_initial.
Call tracker=tracker.descent_step(observations(:,t)) for each column; store tracker.U*tracker.U' at every time, including skipped startup steps.
Store W*W' where W=tracker.samples(:,tracker.window_idx). Store stepsize when active sample count is at least k: fixed alpha or 1/max(4*svd(W)(1)^2,1e-8); otherwise NaN.
Save these outputs to MAT, then use scipy.io.loadmat and numpy.savez_compressed. Standard tests read only NPZ/JSON and require no MATLAB or Octave.

scope.canonical_reference: Root great.m; adapter run_alg.m has a different extreme-small-signal floor and is not the canonical adaptive-step fixture.
scope.comparison: Subspace projectors, raw window covariance and step sizes; Manopt always reorthonormalizes its basis, while the Python code repairs only when needed.
scope.complex: The complex cases pass complex observations and initial bases through the unchanged reference class, whose conjugate-transpose algebra and SVD/QR exponential are numerically defined for these inputs. This does not attribute a native-complex tracking guarantee to the real reference.
